title: Edge SDK binary-size budget quickstart (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a pragmatic, hands-on quickstart for shipping a minimal Redwood SDK build for constrained edge targets (ARMv7/ARM64 Raspberry Pi, Android low-end, WASM for browser IoT). Focus: how to set a binary size budget, measure it, and iterate on API/feature decisions to fit that budget while preserving core ergonomics for developers.

Audience:
- SDK maintainer or engineer owning an edge build
- Solutions engineer prepping a demo on low-power devices
- Product PM evaluating tradeoffs for an embedded offering

Non-goals (for this doc):
- Deep dive into custom toolchains or kernel builds (link out instead)
- Full security or licensing checklist

Quick hypothesis:
If we limit the runtime+client binary to <= 4MB compressed (wasm gzipped) or <= 20MB on-device native (stripped, compressed artifacts), we can support 80% of low-end customer targets without sacrificing streaming/kv-cache semantics.

High-level approach (three passes):
1) Establish a measurable budget + baseline artifact.
2) Prioritize SDK features that must remain vs features that can be offloaded to cloud or omitted.
3) Implement size optimizations (link-time stripping, optional subsystems via feature flags, wasm size tuning).

Step 0 — baseline artifacts (10–30 min)
- Clone minimal example: git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-edge-example
- Build native target (ARM64): docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/work -w /work crossbuild:arm64 ./build-native.sh
- Build wasm: ./build-wasm.sh && gzip -9 -c build/edge_sdk.wasm > build/edge_sdk.wasm.gz
- Measure: ls -lh build/* ; du -sh build/* ; record sizes in the table below (quick mental baseline)

Step 1 — telemetry + measurement contract (required before optimization)
- We need artifact-level measurements checked into CI as a gating metric. Minimal fields to capture as CI artifact: target, uncompressed_size_bytes, compressed_gzip_bytes, symbol_table_count, top-n object sizes.
- Add telemetry to build pipeline: upload size.json to S3 and post to CI dashboard (example script in tools/size-report.sh).
- Acceptance gate: PRs that increase compressed size by >2% require a mitigation plan and explicit reviewer sign-off.

Step 2 — define the SDK surface for the edge binary (decision checklist)
- Required in-core: HTTP transport, token refresh, streaming response consumer, simple prompt batching, small LRU KV cache (on-disk optional).
- Optional-out-of-core: rich telemetry; devtools (local emulator), large format serializers (protobuf heavy schemas), multi-model adapters.
- Export policy: provide 'thin' runtime runtime-only artifact + optional dev bundle that can be installed during development time.

Step 3 — concrete size reduction tactics (order of impact)
- High impact: LTO and strip symbols (native), wasm-opt with -Oz and remove debug info, tree-shake unused code paths during bundling.
- Medium: Replace default JSON library with tiny-json or custom streaming parser, avoid std::vector heavy copies, reduce log strings and avoid fmt heavy usage in hot path.
- Low: Asset compression, reducing icon/fonts in packaged UI, move nonessential constants into remote config.

Engineering checklist (first pass, day 1–3)
- [ ] Baseline builds for armv7, arm64, and wasm recorded in CI
- [ ] Add size-report.sh to build pipeline and post artifacts
- [ ] Feature-flag compilation: BUILD_MINIMAL=true to exclude optional modules
- [ ] Make sure streaming uses callbacks not coroutine heavy frameworks for small binary
- [ ] Add test that runs a small smoke prompt and verifies expected tokens are returned (keeps core behaviour intact)

Developer UX / API thoughts (tradeoffs)
- Keep high-level API identical to hosted SDK but provide two install paths: redwood-edge (tiny) and redwood-dev (full). Clear docs recommended: a note in quickstart.md that redwood-edge does not include the profiler or dev stubs.
- Provide an in-repo shim that maps the full API to a subset on tiny builds — this keeps app code unchanged and fails at runtime with a clear message if a missing function is used.

QA + Acceptance criteria
- Size gate: compressed wasm <= 4MB OR native artifact (stripped tar.gz) <= 20MB for the minimal profile
- Functional gate: basic generation (single prompt), streaming, token counting, and graceful fallback (if KV cache not compiled in) must pass on device with < 1s coldstart on Pi4 (device benchmark target)
- UX gate: quickstart walkthrough for a developer to get a demo running on a Pi (documented in README) in <= 15 minutes using prebuilt artifacts

Rollout plan (beta -> GA)
- Beta: release prebuilt binaries and a small sample app (speech-to-text demo) to internal integrators. Collect telemetry on coldstart and CPU.
- Pilot: 3-5 early customers with low-end devices. Dedicated support channel.
- GA: publish packages (npm wasm package, apt debs for arm64, apk for android) + updated docs.

Open questions / decisions to make
- Do we support local quantized runtime in the tiny build or require remote inference? (cost vs latency tradeoff)
- Where do we put the first-party LTO flags? Repo-level vs per-target?
- CI: which historic baseline do we compare against for regression policies?

Notes to self / follow-ups:
- Talk to infra about CI storage for size artifacts (S3 prefix: s3://redwood-ci/size/edge/)
- Pair with solutions-eng on the Pi4 test matrix (32-bit vs 64-bit)
- Draft a short dev-facing README: INSTALL GUIDE + troubleshooting table for common linker errors

Appendix: quick commands
- wasm build & measure: ./scripts/build-wasm.sh && ./scripts/size-report.sh build/edge_sdk.wasm
- native build & measure: ./scripts/build-native.sh --target=arm64 && ./scripts/size-report.sh build/edge_sdk.tar.gz
- run smoke: QEMU_ARM=1 ./scripts/run-smoke.sh sample-app/config.json

End of draft.
